title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'figures' in a set L. A figure is a family 𝔛 = (X_i)_{i∈I} of subsets indexed by a poset, with the indexing compatible with inclusion. The stratum of X_i is X_i° = X_i minus the union of the members of 𝔛 strictly contained in X_i. The desired axioms are:
(α) every X_i° ≠ ∅;
(β) saturation: X_i = ⋃{X_j° : X_j° ⊂ X_i};
(γ) X_j° ⊂ X_i ⇒ j ≤ i, i.e. X_j ⊂ X_i.
The aim is a combinatorial counterpart of a stratification: a partition into strata indexed by a poset, each X_i being the 'closure' (down-set union) of its own stratum.

The previous page gave an example where α and γ hold but β fails. That example uses a strictly decreasing chain A_0 ⊋ A_1 ⊋ … with N = ⋂A_n ≠ ∅, plus a set A_∞ with A_∞ ∩ A_0 = N and A_∞ ≠ N. There the points of N lie in no stratum, so the A_i are not saturated.

This page asks whether γ is automatic, at least when the indexing respects inclusion. Equivalently: does X_j° ⊂ X_i imply X_j ⊂ X_i? Grothendieck gives a counterexample.
- A first attempt is struck out. It used two strictly decreasing chains (A_i), (B_j) with A_0 ∩ B_0 = ⋂A_i = ⋂B_j = N.
- He then restarts. He keeps the chain (A_i) and A_∞, and adds A = A_∞ − N. The family is 𝔛 = {(A_i), A_∞, A}.

Computing strata:
- The only member strictly inside A_∞ is A, because each A_i ⊄ A_∞ (A_i ∩ A_∞ = N ≠ A_i). So A_∞° = A_∞ − A = N.
- Nothing lies inside A, so A° = A.
- For the chain, A_i° = A_i − A_{i+1}.

The strata A_i − A_{i+1}, N and A are nonempty and pairwise disjoint. Their union is A_0 ∪ A_∞ = A_0 ⊔ A.

The point of adding A is that N is now a stratum. So saturation (β) now holds:
- A_i = ⋃_{j≥i}(A_j − A_{j+1}) ∪ N;
- A_∞ = N ∪ A;
- A = A°.

Yet A_∞° = N ⊂ A_i for every i while A_∞ ⊄ A_i, so γ fails. Hence γ is independent of α, β and disjointness of strata, even for inclusion-compatible indexing. The failure comes from the infinite descending chain: N is the 'limit' stratum, which sits below every A_i in the closure sense, but its 'closure' A_∞ does not.
errors: The machine transcription's A_i° = A_i − A_{i−1} must be A_i − A_{i+1}, since the chain is decreasing; this is the definition used on the previous page.
'A_∞° ⊂ A_i pour i ≠ 0': in fact N ⊂ A_i for all i, including i = 0, so the restriction i ≠ 0 is unnecessary (possibly a slip or misreading). The counterexample is unaffected.

ideas.what: Axioms for a 'figure' (combinatorial stratification of a set): nonempty disjoint strata X_i° defined by removing strictly smaller members; saturation; the condition X_j° ⊂ X_i ⇒ X_j ⊂ X_i (frontier/closure-type condition).
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified sets / Alexandrov-type stratifications; frontier condition for stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Whitney/Thom/Mather frontier condition; Alexandrov topologies); poset-stratified spaces in Lurie's Higher Algebra appendix and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished 1986 'Analysis situs' manuscripts; the theme of stratified 'tame' spaces is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984).

ideas.what: Counterexample, built from an infinite strictly decreasing chain plus an extra 'limit' set, showing that the closure condition (γ) does not follow from nonemptiness, disjointness and saturation of strata.
ideas.modern_name: Independence of axioms for stratifications; failure of finiteness / descending chain condition

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary set-theoretic counterexample used to test the independence of axioms in Grothendieck's combinatorial theory of 'figures'. It is correct and instructive, but routine. Its only interest is as a detail of how he was shaping the axiomatics of tame stratifications in 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'A_i° = A_i − A_{i-1}' should read A_i° = A_i − A_{i+1} (decreasing chain).
'Or a ici' should read 'On a ici'.
'd-t-[?] γ) - avons-nous [?]' is likely 'Dans ... γ) : avons-nous' (asking whether γ holds), but this is uncertain.
'X_j ≤ X_i ⇒ j ≤ i' should read X_j ⊂ X_i ⇒ j ≤ i ('indexation compatible avec les inclusions').
Struck passage: 'Supposons qu'on ait deux familles str. décroissantes, (A_i) comme dessus et B_0 ⊃ B_1 ⊃ …', followed by 'A_0 ∩ B_0 = ⋂A_i = ⋂B_i, soit N' and 'prenons 𝔛 = {A_i, B_j}'.
'un dernier ensemble' likely reads '[on ajoute] un dernier ensemble A = A_∞ − N'.
